reader.title: Killing of Daniel Lee
bases: A prison guard on duty shot and killed a convict he said was escaping from a work detail at the State farm; no crowd was involved (A1, A2, A4).

Two independent Richmond-datelined reports and the Richmond Planet agree that Guard O. D. Traylor shot and killed convict Daniel (Dan) Lee at the State farm, though every account of the circumstances comes from the guard (A1, A2, A4).

summary.text: The killing of Daniel Lee took place on the morning of August 11, 1900, when O. D. Traylor, a guard at the Virginia State farm, shot and killed Lee, a Black convict, with a Winchester rifle.
Traylor said Lee had been trying to escape from a work detail, and the coroner decided that no inquest was needed.
Richmond and Norfolk papers reported the shooting the next day, and the Richmond Planet noted it a week later.
Lee, about forty years old, had been received at the penitentiary from Albemarle County on November 19, 1895, to serve twenty years, ten for housebreaking and ten for malicious assault.
According to the Richmond Times, he had got away once the previous April and was captured the following morning.
Just before 8 o'clock that morning, Traylor took Lee and several other convicts into a field and set Lee to raking grass along the edge of a ditch.
In the account the Times published, Traylor turned away to instruct the other men, then saw Lee about twenty-five yards off, moving in a crouch along the ditch toward a stand of woods.
The guard said he called on Lee twice to halt, then raised his rifle and fired.
Lee fell face down in the ditch and died at once; the Virginian-Pilot said he was shot through the heart.
Traylor reported the shooting, Lee's body was carried back to the house, and the coroner was notified.
After being told the facts, the coroner decided that an inquest was not necessary.
No report of charges against the guard was found.
Every account of the shooting came from the guard's side.

The Richmond Times headlined it "Prisoner Killed by His Guard" with the deck "Escaping Convict Shot Down in His Wild Dash for Freedom," and opened by saying the killing illustrated the "vigilance" of the State farm guards and the "futility of attempting to escape."
The Virginian-Pilot ran the story as "Negro Instantly Killed" inside its Richmond letter, between a heat wave and state politics, and stated the escape attempt as fact.
The Fredericksburg Free Lance gave it one sentence in its "Current Topics" column on August 16.
The Richmond Planet, a Black weekly, carried a single line among its personals on August 18.
Unlike the white papers, it attributed the escape claim to the guard, writing that "He alleges that Lee was trying to escape," and added that "the jury exonerated him."
Accounts differ on whether any inquiry was held.

Both Richmond-datelined reports, published the day after the shooting, said the coroner found no inquest necessary, while the Planet's later item referred to a jury that exonerated Traylor without giving details.
No other report of a jury proceeding was found.

accounts.label: Guard's account (Richmond reports)
accounts.gist: Traylor turned his back on Lee for a moment; Lee ran crouching along a ditch toward woods, ignored two calls to halt, and was shot dead with one rifle shot.

accounts.label: Black correspondent
accounts.gist: Traylor 'alleges' Lee was trying to escape, and a jury exonerated him.

framing.detail: The Richmond Times headlined 'Prisoner Killed by His Guard / Escaping Convict Shot Down in His Wild Dash for Freedom' and opened by calling the killing an illustration of the guards' 'vigilance' and the 'futility of attempting to escape'.
The Virginian-Pilot ran it as 'Negro Instantly Killed' inside a Richmond letter, stating the escape attempt as fact; the Free Lance gave it one sentence.
The Richmond Planet gave it one line among personals, attributing the escape claim to the guard ('He alleges').

versions.value: The coroner decided an inquest was not necessary
